messages:
eva: Quick heads-up from onboarding: noticed inconsistent request-id propagation across sampleapp SDK variants. Node shows X-Request-Id in logs, Python shows it only in spans (as baggage), and Go sometimes drops it across async handlers. Repro notes below.

mike: that's bad for debugging. Do we map X-Request-Id into OTEL baggage anywhere, or rely on trace context?

hannah: In sampleapp we accidentally relied on different defaults: Node code maps `req.headers['x-request-id']` into `baggage.set` during middleware, Python sample does not. Go uses the incoming header only if `OTEL_PROPAGATORS` includes `baggage`. So parity is broken.

ryan: TL;DR: mismatched propagators + ad-hoc header-copying = flaky request-id lineage. Which environments reproduce this?

eva: Local dev and staging. Quick repro: send request with `X-Request-Id: r-abc` and call an async queue handler. Node logs keep reqId. Python spans show `baggage.request_id=r-abc` but logs lack it. Go logs sometimes lose it after `go func()` boundary.

mike: likely because Node middleware does `baggage.setBag(ctx, { request_id })` while Python sample uses `context.attach` only for traces. Also `OTEL_PROPAGATORS` in our CI is set to `tracecontext`, not `tracecontext,baggage`, so the baggage header isn't parsed consistently.

hannah: good catch. We should standardize on W3C `traceparent` + `baggage` and document that sampleapps must set `OTEL_PROPAGATORS=tracecontext,baggage` for full parity. Also add an explicit mapping layer that copies X-Request-Id <-> baggage.request_id at the ingress middleware to avoid depending on propagator order.

ryan: agree. Two changes: (1) docs + quickstart env recommendation, (2) small middleware shim in all sampleapps that does:```js
// ingress shim (Node)
const ctx = propagation.extract(defaultTextMapGetter, req.headers);
const bag = propagation.getBaggage(ctx) || createEmptyBaggage();
const requestId = req.headers['x-request-id'] || bag.getEntry('request_id')?.value || nanoid();
const newBag = setBaggageEntry(bag, 'request_id', requestId);
const ctx2 = propagation.setBaggage(ctx, newBag);
context.with(ctx2, () => next());
```
This ensures logs and spans see the same id.

mike: for Python and Go we should implement equivalent shim. Also update sampleapp smoke test to assert that a request-id survives a queued async job and shows up in logs/spans.

hannah: one more subtlety: some ingress proxies also inject `x-amzn-trace-id` or `x-cloud-trace-context`. We should canonicalize: prefer `X-Request-Id` header, then baggage.request_id, then common cloud headers. Add that to the doc.

ryan: I'll open an INF ticket with a minimal repro across SDKs and link to sampleapp PR. Anyone want to take the Node shim?

eva: I can wire the Node shim and add the smoke test. I'll also add a devex doc explaining why OTEL_PROPAGATORS must include `baggage` for request-id parity.

mike: great. For longer term, consider instrumenting our logging library to read baggage from current context automatically when formatting logs, so callers don't have to pass reqId everywhere. But opt-in only.

hannah: agree but don't auto-enable in sampleapps yet; opt-in avoids surprises and redaction issues. Add a note about respecting redaction: middleware should sanitize baggage values before logging.

telemetry-bot: Created ticket DEVEX-3607: "SDK parity: request-id propagation inconsistent across Node/Python/Go -> add ingress shim + docs" https://tracker/redwood/DEVEX-3607

eva: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sampleapp/pull/140 with Node shim + smoke test. Will add matching TODOs for python/go.

mike: thanks. Once PR lands update onboarding.md and add a CI smoke job that runs the cross-SDK repro matrix. That should cut onboarding noise.

hannah: final note: include a short section in the DX docs on `OTEL_PROPAGATORS` gotchas and how baggage relates to headers vs logs. Newcomers keep assuming `traceparent` carries request-id. It doesn't.

eva: will do. Thanks all.
